DISTRICT INDORE (MADHYA PRADESH)
 ..
 (SHRI VIRAJ GODHA-PANEL LAWYER FOR RESPONDENT/STATE)
 (SHRI VIKAS YADAV, ADVOCATE FOR OBJECTOR)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the co  following:
 ORDER Heard and perused the case diary.

This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.08/2023, registered at P.S.- Crime Branch,
Indore, District- Indore (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 409, 120-B, of IPC, 1860 and Section 66-D of Information and Technology Act, 2000.
He is in custody since 01.04.2023.

sentences.text:
As per the prosecution story, the allegations against the applicant is that he is involved in the aforesaid offence where a sum of Rs.22,19,000/- approximately has been misappropriated by the accused persons by promising the investors for higher returns and later on deprived of the same.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been implicated only on the basis of memorandum of co- accused Milan recorded under Section 27 of Evidence Act.

The applicant is ready to pay the one fourth amount of the total misappropriation amount i.e. Rs.22,19,000/-The applicant is in jail since 01.04.2023 and conclusion of trial will take considerable time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant/accused be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection.
5. Counsel for the objector/complainants has vehemently opposed the prayer by stating that considering the seriousness of the offence the applicant is not entitled for grant of bail.
However, it is fairly contended that if the applicant deposits the one fourth part of the total misappropriated amount, the objector/complainants have no objection in releasing the applicant on bail.

6. In view of the aforesaid arguments, looking to the custody period and also looking to the fact that the applicant is ready to deposit the one fourth part of the misappropriated amount i.e. Rs.7.40 lakhs, without reflecting anything on the merits of the case, the application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. on behalf of the applicant is hereby allowed subject to deposit a sum of Rs.7,40,000/-
(Rupees Seven lakhs and forty thousand only) by the applicant or any other person on his behalf,
out of which, Rs.5,50,000/-
(Rupees five Lakhs and fifty thousand) before his release i.e. at the time of furnishing the bail bond in a fixed deposit in a nationalized bank and producing the receipt/certificate of the same before the concerned trial Court and rest of Rs.1,90,000/- (Rupees one lakh and ninety thousand only) to be deposited by the applicant within a period of three months from the date of his release in a fixed deposit in a nationalized bank and producing the receipt/certificate of the same before the concerned trial Court.

7. It is directed that, the applicant shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties (out of which one local surety)
of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the trial Court, to appear before the trial Court on the dates given by the Court.

The applicant shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
8 .

The complainants namely Jitendra Soni, Sandeep Joshi and Narendra Dave are permitted to withdraw the amount so deposited by the petitioner subject to furnishing appropriate surety in the like amount before the trial court against the aforesaid amount.

Learned counsel for the aforesaid complainants has given undertaking that he shall file an affidavit of the complainants regarding returning of the whole amount so withdrawn, if the case will be decided in favour of the applicant.
